_comment: EXAMPLE. Copy to model_routes.json and edit — the real file is gitignored,
like .env. The INTERNAL NAMES are the repo's contract: agent_configs and the
vision gate and novel pipelines reference `flash` / `glm` / `smart` /
`novel` / `novel_alt` / `vision`, so those keys
must exist. WHICH endpoints serve them is entirely yours — the lists below
are one operator's answer, not a requirement. (A `pro` route used to sit
here; it was deleted once its candidate list and `smart`'s had become the
same, and no agent_config names it.)
Internal model name -> ordered list of concrete provider/model endpoints.
An agent_config's `model` (and the vision gate's judge) names one of these;
AIGateway binds the first candidate and falls over to the next ONLY on an
endpoint error (401/403 dead key or lapsed plan, 429 quota/rate limit, 5xx,
connection loss). A bad request or an oversized context is NOT failed over
— every candidate would reject it the same way.

STICKY within a step; a dict-form route {"rotate": [...], "fallback": [...]} additionally rotates its pool head once per STEP so several plans' windows all get used — fallback (pay-as-you-go) never rotates forward.
step's turns hit one endpoint. Provider prefix caches are per-provider and
this workload is 26:1 prefill:decode at an 89.4% hit rate; alternating
endpoints per call converts cached input into full-price input and costs
more than any token plan saves. Spread quota per RUN, not per call.
A spent usage window parks that ONE provider/model until the provider's
stated reset instant, so the plans below are consumed in order and a spent
one is skipped outright rather than re-probed once per step.
Providers referenced here must exist in llm_providers.json, and their key
file must exist in ~/.aitelier-secrets/ (whole dir is mounted; no compose edit). Names not listed
here pass through unchanged if they contain a '/', so a concrete
provider/model still works in an agent_config with no entry.
_ordering_note: Every route ends with a `deepseek/` PAY-AS-YOU-GO candidate on purpose. A
token plan can run out; pay-as-you-go cannot, so it is the only thing that
makes 'both plans are spent' a slowdown instead of a stop. ark and qwen are
separate plans with separate windows, so they are consumed in order and a
spent one is parked, not re-probed.
How much a failover changes, per route:
* flash — NOTHING but the bill. Same family, different door. (Caveat: qwen
serves DATED snapshots, deepseek-v4-flash-0731, where ark serves a
rolling alias and api.deepseek.com serves whatever `deepseek-flash`
currently means; they drift when DeepSeek ships a new model. See
* glm — degrades. 5.2 is genuinely older than 5.3, and the last candidate
* smart / vision — a different model outright. See their notes.
So `served_by` in the trace is not bookkeeping: for three of the four routes
it is what tells you whether a result is evidence about the model you think
_worker_note: DSH native subagents use worker; each child rotates once, then keeps a sticky provider for its tool turns. Configure the deployment pool independently of the director's model. The pay-as-you-go fallback is what lets an install holding only DEEPSEEK_API_KEY dispatch workers.
_flash_review_note: Reviewer roles (the *_reviewer roles that used to ride `flash`) name their own
route so a deployment can staff review apart from implementation. Measured
2026-10-08 by replaying 6 recorded implementation reviews on the commits they
reviewed (2 samples each; 5 carry defects confirmed by the next commit or by
reading the code): confirmed defects named out of 10 - DeepSeek V4.1-Flash at
effort high 9, Claude Sonnet 5.5 high 9, V4.1 low 7, Haiku 5.5 high 6,
GLM-5.3-Flash low 4 and high 4, Haiku low 3, Sonnet low 0. GLM is not a rubber
stamp - it catches what is visible in the files it reads - but misses defects
that need cross-file or engine reasoning, and effort does not change that. On
Claude, effort governs how much it checks: never staff a reviewer at low.
This example keeps the same candidates as `flash` so a clean checkout starts.
_deepseek_ids_note: Read off api-docs.deepseek.com on 2026-09-11. Two of the ids above are
ALIASES, and a completion cannot tell you which model served it — the
response's `model` field only echoes the request.
* On api.deepseek.com, `deepseek-flash` IS DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. The older
`deepseek-v4-flash` / `-vision-exp` ids still answer, but those models
are RETIRED and their requests are served by V4.1 at the Flash price.
Other providers host their OWN snapshots and are not party to that, so
`ark/deepseek-v4-flash` is still a V4 model.
* From 12:00 Beijing time 2026-09-14, `deepseek-v4-pro` on
api.deepseek.com is ALSO served by V4.1-Flash, billed at the Flash
price, until V4.1-Pro ships. It is `smart`'s last candidate below, so
from that date a failover there quietly demotes a pro-class role to a
flash model under a name that still says pro. Check `served_by`.
* Effort is a 3-way switch, not a dial: the vendor maps minimal/low->low,
medium/high/xhigh->high, max/ultra->max. Thinking is ON by default at
`high`, so declaring nothing is not the cheap option.
* Whether an effort declaration reaches the model is PER MODEL, not per
provider — on one reseller the same key is honoured by one DeepSeek
model and ignored by another. Measure with effort `none`/low/high on a
fixed prompt before trusting a route's `effort` block.
_glm_note: The last candidate is a DIFFERENT FAMILY, not another door to GLM. That is
a real behaviour change and it is the point: without it, both token plans
running out leaves every glm role with nowhere to go and the run stops. A
DeepSeek answer is a worse GLM answer than GLM's; it is a far better one
than no answer. Check `served_by` in the trace before reading a glm-role
_smart_note: qwen3.8-max: a 2.4T MoE (95B active), 262K context, native vision, its own
low/medium/xhigh effort scale. NOT interchangeable with the others, so it
is its own route and no existing role has been moved onto it.
What the independent evidence supports (Aug 2026): elite ALGORITHMIC coding
and tool use (LMArena Code #3), GPQA reproduced at 92.6% vs a claimed 92.7%.
What it does NOT support: the agentic numbers. Terminal-Bench 2.1 does not
replicate under a neutral harness, it sits #15/55 on the Coding Agent Index
with an 11-point SWE-bench gap to Opus 5, and agentic coding is its worst
LiveBench category. It is also reported unreliable on facts, and to
'default to wildly overthinking' — pin the effort if you use it.
Read against this pipeline: that profile fits the ONE-SHOT judgement steps
(the *_review reviewers, the architect, the PM) and argues AGAINST t_impl,
which is a 24-turn agentic tool loop — its worst category — and against the
researcher, which must not invent facts. Measure before moving any role:
replay the step against ~/.AItelier/scratch/effort_ab/ rather than trusting
this paragraph.
The fallbacks are a DIFFERENT model, so a failover here changes behaviour,
not just the bill. That is the right trade for availability, but it means a
run served by the fallback is not evidence about qwen3.8-max — check
`served_by` in the trace before drawing a conclusion.
_novel_note: `novel` and `novel_alt` are separate stable role contracts: prose makers
use `novel`; prose reviewers and rewriters use `novel_alt`. The example
reuses public endpoints already declared by `flash` and `glm`; it does not
publish or constrain any deployment's private endpoint ordering or effort.
A deployment may replace both candidate lists, but must keep both aliases
and must not silently map either one to the code/reasoning `smart` route.
_vision_note: ONE judge. The hosted candidates were removed 2026-08-26, measured:
neither ever finished a run — two attempts, both blind (4 of 47 scenarios,
then 12) — because a batch is ~4.7 MB of base64 and this host uploads to
them at 14 KB/s: 5.5 min per request, ~4.3 hours for a round. That is
longer than the gap between container rebuilds during development, so the
run was killed and restarted from scenario 1 every time, and it spent the
same 5-hour provider quota the pipeline needs (which killed a run outright
at 00:44 that day). The local vLLM does all 47 scenarios in ~10 min.
When it is not serving, the call is refused in milliseconds, the gate goes
`blind`, and the graph routes to the 5_vision_human checkpoint where a
person answers the six questions in minutes. Waiting four hours to reach
that same checkpoint is strictly worse.
_input_note: What each CONCRETE candidate can be sent: `text`, or `text` and `image`.
A candidate missing here takes text only. A route takes images only when
EVERY candidate it resolves to lists `image`, because a bad request is not
failed over: a failover onto a text-only candidate would make that turn a
400. A project whose `model` is a concrete provider/model is looked up the
same way. Fill an entry only after that candidate was seen reading the text
in an image sent through AIGateway (the path /completion uses); a vendor
page saying 'vision supported' is not a measurement.
List EVERY candidate of every route, `["text"]` for the unmeasured ones:
once `_input` exists it holds for the whole table, and the backend's
startup line names any candidate it lacks as `unlisted (text-only)`. That
set is empty for this example.
What the image entries below rest on (2026-11-23, one AIGateway call per
candidate: a 64x32 PNG reading '4721', then a full A4 page of Chinese
rendered from an image-only PDF):
* ollamacloud/deepseek-v4.1-flash — read both.
* opencodego/deepseek-v4.1-flash — INFERRED: this account's quota was
spent; two other accounts on the same endpoint and model id read both.
* deepseek/deepseek-flash — reads images because AIGateway sends a
request that carries one on the `openai/` path (same api_base, same
key); the native deepseek path drops them.
* localqwen/qwen3 — the vision judge, which reads screenshots every run.
So `driver`, `worker`, `steward`, `novel` and `vision` take images. Every
`["text"]` entry is unmeasured, not refused — qwen3.8-max's native vision
included — so `flash`, `flash_review`, `glm`, `smart` and `novel_alt` are
text-only here until someone measures.
_steward_note: `route` and its `child_route`). It reads photos and PDF page images, so
EVERY candidate here must list `image` in `_input`: one text-only
candidate makes the whole route text-only, and the steward process then
logs it and flags '管家路线不收图' on its dashboard status. It ends with the
pay-as-you-go candidate like every other route.
